name: Samuel N. Hazen

career.title: Financial Management Specialist Program trainee, then hospital and regional CFO roles
Chief Financial Officer, North Texas Division
Chief Operating Officer; President and COO from November 2016

background_rationale: He began in Humana's financial management training program and spent his first two decades in hospital, division and group CFO roles before moving into operations leadership at HCA.

notable.summary: HCA completed its purchase of Mission Health, the Asheville, North Carolina-based hospital system.
HCA finalized a partnership with Google to develop healthcare algorithms using patient records.

Reporting Q4 2025 results, HCA authorized an additional $10 billion share repurchase program and guided to 2026 revenue of $76.5-80.0 billion, with Hazen citing investments in network expansion and workforce development.
HCA lowered its full-year 2026 guidance after a shift in payer mix toward uninsured patients cost about $400 million in the second quarter.

personal_story.hook: Sam Hazen started in a Humana finance trainee program and rose through hospital CFO jobs to run HCA.
personal_story.summary: Hazen earned a business degree from the University of Kentucky in 1982 and began his healthcare career in Humana's Financial Management Specialist Program. He worked as a chief financial officer at hospitals, including in Georgia and Las Vegas, and also earned an MBA from the University of Nevada, Las Vegas. After joining HCA's North Texas division as CFO in 1994, he became CFO and then president of its Western Group, which he ran for a decade before moving up to run operations companywide. He became CEO in January 2019 and has said the lessons that guided him are hard work, continued learning and treating people right, which he credits to his parents.

facts.label: Turning point
facts.value: Named president of HCA's Western Group in 2001, overseeing roughly half the company's revenue

facts.label: Family background
facts.value: Credits his parents with teaching him to treat people right

facts.label: Other
facts.value: Inducted into the University of Kentucky Gatton College Alumni Hall of Fame in 2016

quote.text: The third thing my parents taught me — pretty basic stuff, but it has powerful implications — is just to treat people right.
quote.context: On the '3 Takeaways' podcast with Lynn Thoman, December 2024
